comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C36-C38, C52 regarding reciprocal dependency between GNU and BIC-C for granule localization. Both evaluations find the data well-supported without substantive critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C41, C56 regarding evidence against the sequestration model and support for the beacon model. Both acknowledge the data support this interpretation, though OpenEval notes the model remains somewhat speculative based on exclusion rather than direct demonstration, while peer reviewers accept it as a reasonable creative interpretation.
Perfect agreement on claim C14 regarding PP2A enrichment in mass spectrometry data. Both accept this finding without critique, though both note the functional connection is not experimentally tested.
Perfect agreement on claims C58-C62 regarding evolutionary conservation with the NEK7/BICC1/ANKS system. Both accept this comparative analysis as reasonable based on literature citations.

Strong agreement on claims C18-C22 regarding gnu∆SAM phenotypes and protein persistence. Both find the data well-supported. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretation is inferential; peer reviewers only request improved figure presentation without questioning conclusions.

Strong agreement on claims C30-C31, C48, C50 regarding GNU9A phosphorylation effects. Both find data supported. OpenEval explicitly notes mechanistic interpretation is speculative; peer reviewers accept the interpretation without direct critique.

Strong agreement on claims C24-C26 regarding GNU dispersal after activation and lack of PNG/PLU granular localization. Both evaluations accept these localization findings as clear evidence without substantive critique.

Agreement on claims C5, C55, C57 being speculative models. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct evidence; peer reviewers also note interpretations are speculative and beacon model not yet proven, but accept as reasonable hypothesis given paper scope.

Strong agreement on core claims C3, C12-C13, C23, C42-C43 regarding GNU as RNP granule component. Both find data clear and convincing. OpenEval covers broader claim set (C27-C29, C32-C33, C44-C45) also addressing granule localization; peer review focuses on subset establishing the key finding.

Partial overlap on claims C27-C29, C44 regarding GNU co-localization with RNP markers. Both find data supported. Peer reviewers request improved figure presentation (high magnification insets) but accept underlying conclusions, consistent with OpenEval's SUPPORTED evaluation.

Disagreement on claims C16-C17 (also C15 in peer review) regarding GNU9A and SAM domain role. OpenEval finds well-supported despite some speculation; peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation, requesting quantification and normalization of GNU9A data in immunoprecipitation experiments.

Partial overlap on claims C32-C33, C45 regarding GNU∆SAM localization. Both find data supported. Peer reviewers request improved figure presentation for co-localization images but do not question data quality, consistent with OpenEval's inclusion in broader SUPPORTED evaluation.

Agreement on claim C54 regarding RNP granule heterogeneity. Both find this interpretation supported by co-localization data. Peer reviewer suggests additional citation (Niepielko et al. 2018), indicating agreement with conclusion.

Agreement on claim C51 regarding GNU recruitment timing to BIC-C granules. Both accept this as reasonable inference based on literature citations, though OpenEval notes recruitment dynamics not directly observed in this study.

Minimal overlap on claim C46 regarding SAM domain requirement. OpenEval includes in SUPPORTED evaluation of SAM domain role; peer reviewers accept without specific critique in their broader evaluation.
Minimal overlap on claim C53 regarding decreased BIC-C levels in gnu∆SAM. OpenEval notes this is documented but mechanism unclear; peer reviewers accept without specific critique.

Minimal overlap on claim C49 regarding SAM domain as main mechanism. OpenEval notes this includes speculative interpretation but overall SUPPORTED; peer reviewers group with broader speculative interpretations rated UNCERTAIN.

OpenEval result R12 covers extensive background claims C1-C2, C6-C11, C63-C89 from literature, finding them accurately represented. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background claims.
